subject: history_social
passage: Many companies have replaced private offices and cubicles with open-plan workspaces in which employees sit at shared tables with no walls between them. Supporters argue that removing the walls increases face-to-face conversation among coworkers, since people can see one another and simply walk over to talk. Management researcher Leila Haddad calls this the open interaction hypothesis.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the open interaction hypothesis?

choices.A: Employees in open-plan offices reported that they could overhear their coworkers' conversations throughout the working day.
choices.B: At a company that switched to an open plan, employees were observed walking over to colleagues' desks several times each hour.
choices.C: After one company switched to an open plan, sensors worn by employees recorded a sharp drop in face-to-face conversation.
choices.D: Open-plan offices cost less to build and maintain than offices divided into private rooms, and they hold more workers.

explanation.why: The hypothesis predicts more face-to-face conversation once walls are removed. To weaken it, a finding must show that face-to-face conversation did not increase, or actually fell, after a switch to an open plan. Measurements showing a sharp drop in conversation do exactly that.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Overhearing others is not the same as talking with them more, so this does not test the hypothesis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Frequent visits to colleagues' desks would support the hypothesis rather than weaken it.
explanation.C: Correct. Less face-to-face conversation after the walls came down is the opposite of what the hypothesis predicts, so this finding weakens it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Cost has nothing to do with whether people talk face-to-face more often.
